title: Java Slide 2
description: Practice examination covering Java comments, class declarations, identifiers, standard I/O, Scanner, printf, escape sequences, arithmetic expressions, operator precedence, and decision-making statements.

questions.prompt: What is the exact printed output when the following Java program is compiled and executed?
questions.explanation: Java is case-sensitive so a1 and A1 are distinct variables, underscores in numeric literals are ignored, and destructive assignment overwrites a1 with 2000 before A1 is overwritten with 500.

questions.prompt: What is the exact printed output when the following Java program is compiled and executed?
questions.explanation: System.out.print keeps the cursor on the same line, the traditional comment /* ... */ is ignored by the compiler, \" prints a double quote, and \\ prints a single backslash.

questions.prompt: What is the exact printed output when the following Java program is compiled and executed?
questions.explanation: Integer division (19 / 5) truncates the fractional part without rounding to yield 3, while the remainder operator (19 % 5) yields the leftover value 4.

questions.prompt: Assume the following complete source file InputTest.java is compiled with javac InputTest.java. What is the exact compile-time result?

options.text: Compile-time error: cannot find symbol class System because java.lang is not imported
Compile-time error: method main must return an int value instead of void
Compile-time error: cannot find symbol class Scanner because java.util.Scanner is not imported
Compile-time error: variable value must be declared before creating the Scanner object
Compile-time error: System.in cannot be passed as an argument to new Scanner

questions.explanation: Classes in java.lang such as System are imported by default, but using Scanner without an import java.util.Scanner; declaration before the class causes a 'cannot find symbol' compilation error.

questions.prompt: What is the exact line of text displayed when the following Java program is compiled and executed?
questions.explanation: Before \r, printf outputs the 10-character string 'Java-AB-11'; the carriage return \r moves the cursor to the start of the line, and 'JDK-AB' overwrites only the first 6 characters ('Java-A'), leaving 'B-11' at the end.

questions.prompt: What is the exact printed output when the following Java program is compiled and executed?
questions.explanation: Innermost parentheses evaluate first (b + c = 7, then 25 % 7 = 4), multiplicative operators associate left-to-right (25 / 4 = 6, 6 * 4 = 24, and 4 / 2 = 2), and additive operators associate left-to-right (25 - 24 + 2 = 3).

questions.prompt: What is the exact printed output when the following Java program is compiled and executed?
questions.explanation: The semicolon after if (x > y); creates an empty body so x = x + 15 always executes (making x = 25); then x < y (25 < 20) is false, which skips only the single unbraced statement y = y + 10 while x = x + 5 still executes.

questions.prompt: Assume the user enters 23 followed by 5 at the keyboard. What is the exact printed output of the following program?
questions.explanation: Integer division 23 / 5 truncates to 4 before adding 5, destructively assigning 9 to $val_1; the next statement uses this updated value to compute 9 % 5 = 4 for _val2.

questions.prompt: What is the exact printed output when the following Java program is compiled and executed?
questions.explanation: Right-to-left assignment sets both a and d to 3 (7 - 4); in the first if, relational '>' has higher precedence than '==', so (5 > 7) == (2 > 2) evaluates to false == false which is true (updating a to 13), and in the second if, (3 <= 13) != (7 >= 13) evaluates to true != false which is also true (updating d to 23).

questions.prompt: What is the exact line of text displayed when the following Java program is compiled and executed?
questions.explanation: Initially p = 2 + 3 = 5, the first if updates p to 9, and the semicolon after the second if forces p = p * 2 to execute unconditionally (making p = 18); printf first outputs 'p=4, m=14' (using n=4 first), and then '\rp=18' overwrites the first 4 characters ('p=4,'), erasing the comma to leave 'p=18 m=14'.
